catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Structural and domain architectural extraction targeting cas_runner runtime and cas-knowledge persistence, excluding agentic/prompt orchestration.

system_map.overview: cas_runner is a Python-based continuous architecture management platform structured around domain entity modeling, transition registries, and layered file-based knowledge repository management.

patterns.name: Typed Domain Entity Modeling via Pydantic
patterns.summary: Core enterprise architecture entities and governance artifacts are formalized using Pydantic BaseModel instances to enforce rigid data schemas and automated serialization.
patterns.intent: Ensure all architectural data artifacts exchanged across the application and persisted to disk maintain deterministic structural validation and type guarantees.
patterns.context: The system processes architecture models, compliance metrics, git deltas, and governance records from external files and operational workflows.
forces: Schema drift between stored markdown/yaml records and in-memory execution
Need for automatic serialization and deserialization across CLI and dashboard components
patterns.solution: Define data structures (such as GovernanceInventory, ComplianceMetrics, and SteeringRuntimeIndex) as explicit Pydantic domain models with strongly typed attributes.
implementation_signals: Imports of BaseModel, Field from pydantic in domain model files
Domain classes representing business entities such as ResolutionResult, CapabilityRecord, and ComplianceFinding

evidence.note: Models governance entities and metrics using typed Pydantic models.
Models capability catalogs and git steering state as Pydantic entities.

benefits: Self-documenting domain model via Python type annotations
Validation catches malformed input at the system boundary
costs: Runtime validation overhead on massive artifact trees
Coupling of domain definitions to the Pydantic library
failure_modes: Validation errors raised unexpectedly if persisted schema formats mutate without backward compatibility

patterns.reuse_notes: Use across all domain models that deserialize external state or report data across application boundaries.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Management
patterns.summary: Decouples state transition handlers and governance action lifecycles through an explicit transition registry table or container.
patterns.intent: Allow dynamic registration and lookup of governance action state transitions without monolithic branching statements.
patterns.context: Governance actions transition across states (e.g. pending, resolved, rejected, exception) governed by configurable lifecycle rules.
forces: Monolithic if/else cascades make lifecycle expansion brittle
Need to register new domain state transitions without modifying the action evaluation engine
patterns.solution: Encapsulate available state changes inside a TransitionRegistry that pairs valid source states, target states, and execution handlers.
implementation_signals: Methods for registering and invoking transitions based on action state

evidence.note: TransitionRegistry maintains valid state transitions for GovernanceActionEngine.

benefits: Open/Closed principle adherence for governance lifecycle states
Isolation of transition pre-conditions and validation logic
costs: Indirect dispatch adds call stack depth
Requires upfront initialization of registered handlers
failure_modes: Unregistered transitions can lead to runtime exceptions if lookup fails

patterns.reuse_notes: Appropriate for any stateful domain entity governed by workflow or compliance status transitions.

patterns.name: File-Tree Knowledge Repository Persistence
patterns.summary: Uses a structured, version-controlled directory hierarchy as the canonical persistence engine for architectural decisions, rules, and runtime evaluations.
patterns.intent: Store architectural state and governance models as plain text (Markdown, YAML, JSON) files directly under git version control.
patterns.context: Continuous architecture governance mandates auditability, diffability, and offline editing of decisions, metrics, and templates.
forces: Relational databases isolate architecture knowledge from code repositories
Architectural governance artifacts must be reviewable in standard pull requests
patterns.solution: Structure persistence around standard path conventions (e.g., cas-knowledge/global, cas-knowledge/projects, cas-knowledge/runtime) reading and writing artifacts using structured file serializers.
implementation_signals: Directory structures partitioning global/, governance/, projects/, runtime/, and templates/
Bootstrap operations merging workspaces and initializing standard repository templates

evidence.note: Initializes and merges governance files and directory scaffolding into the local workspace.

benefits: Native git history, branching, and pull request integration
Zero operational overhead for external database clusters
Human readability of persisted architecture states
costs: Filesystem I/O contention during high-frequency parallel updates
Lack of transactional ACID locks across multi-file operations
failure_modes: File schema corruption or parse failures if manual edits violate required markdown frontmatter or YAML schemas

patterns.reuse_notes: Well-suited for GitOps platforms and local-first architecture repositories.

patterns.name: Provider Client Adapter
patterns.summary: Abstracts external provider SDK calls behind dedicated client classes with drop-in test doubles.
patterns.intent: Decouple domain and application logic from third-party vendor interfaces and enable deterministic local testing without external API calls.
patterns.context: The system relies on external SDKs for upstream processing (e.g., LiteLLM), but internal engines and automated CI tests require offline deterministic execution.
forces: Direct imports of external client libraries couple business services to vendor SDKs
CI pipelines require offline hermetic test runs
patterns.solution: Wrap external client interactions inside dedicated client classes (e.g. LiteLLMClient) paired with interchangeable mock implementations (MockLLMClient).
implementation_signals: Co-located client implementations and mock clients exposing identical call interfaces
Configuration switches or injection passing client instances to runners

evidence.note: Provides deterministic test double adhering to the client interface.

benefits: Single point of modification for external provider upgrades or telemetry wrapping
costs: Adapter maintenance when external upstream APIs change
failure_modes: Mock divergence if MockLLMClient behavior drifts from actual LiteLLMClient behavior

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard adapter pattern applicable across any third-party infrastructure integration.

patterns.name: Pure Functional Health Evaluation Heuristic
patterns.summary: Computes composite health metrics and evaluation reasons through stateless, pure functional calculations derived from metric aggregates.
patterns.intent: Prevent state mutation and side-effects during architectural health audits by calculating status purely from input metrics.
patterns.context: Dashboards and CLI tools need to assess system architectural health based on compliance metrics, risks, and unresolved exceptions.
forces: Mutable calculation logic inside UI models risks inconsistent reporting
Health aggregation logic must be easily unit tested in isolation
patterns.solution: Structure evaluation as pure functions that receive metric models and return deterministic HealthStatus enums and explanation lists.
implementation_signals: Standalone functions calculate_health and get_health_reasons taking metric schemas as arguments
Use of explicit HealthStatus enum results

evidence.note: Implements pure functional evaluation of health state based on metric findings.

benefits: Trivial unit testability without mock frameworks
Referential transparency across CLI and web dashboards
costs: Requires passing all context parameters explicitly to the calculation function
failure_modes: Incomplete input metric models lead to partial health evaluations

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable across governance reporting and diagnostic scoring engines.

patterns.name: Service Facade Orchestration
patterns.summary: Encapsulates multi-step governance actions and compliance evaluations behind cohesive application service interfaces.
patterns.intent: Provide coarse-grained operations for runners and CLI entry points while coordinating domain models and compliance engines.
patterns.context: CLI commands and automated workflows require running governance assessments without dealing directly with raw state registries or individual file parsers.
forces: Presentation components become bloated if orchestrating multiple domain operations
Transaction and execution logic should be reusable across automated and manual triggers
patterns.solution: Expose application services such as GovernanceActionService and ComplianceEngine to orchestrate operations.
implementation_signals: Cohesive service classes providing high-level operations for governance execution
Delegation from CLI and runner to service classes

evidence.note: Coordinates governance actions, resolutions, and lifecycle execution.
Evaluates rules and findings into unified compliance metrics.

benefits: Separation of concerns between orchestration and presentation
Single entry point for auditing workflow execution
costs: Additional indirection layer between presentation and domain logic
failure_modes: Risk of services devolving into god classes if domain logic is not pushed into domain entities

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard application layer pattern for complex domain workflows.

anti_patterns.name: Direct Filesystem Entanglement
symptoms: Direct pathlib or os.path calls scattered inside business rule checks rather than behind an abstract storage interface
Hardcoded relative directory paths (cas-knowledge/global) in application logic
impact: Inability to run in-memory testing without actual disk writes
Fragile behavior across differing operating systems or cloud deployment environments
suggested_remediation: Introduce a KnowledgeRepository or FileStore abstraction defining read/write contracts
Inject storage providers into ComplianceEngine and GovernanceActionService

anti_patterns.name: Anemic Domain Models with External Engines
symptoms: Pydantic models act strictly as data containers without domain invariants or behavioral methods
All business logic centralized inside engine services operating on bare model attributes
impact: Business rules become fragmented across different service implementations
Invalid intermediate model states can be created without triggering validation errors
suggested_remediation: Encapsulate domain state transitions and validation rules directly inside Pydantic model methods or domain aggregate roots

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Observability and Distributed Tracing
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Integration of OpenTelemetry API and SDK (opentelemetry-api, opentelemetry-sdk in pyproject.toml) to track flow execution, run spans, and governance latency.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Documentation Site Generation
cross_cutting_concerns.description: MkDocs material integration with drawing and link plugins to render architectural knowledge repositories as readable portals.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent filesystem writes coordinated when multiple actions run in parallel?
open_questions.context: The cas-knowledge directory appears to rely on plain file structures without apparent file-locking or optimistic concurrency controls in the model definitions.
